ip_top_stories.title: DOJ's OpenAI Copyright Brief Previews AI Licensing Deals' Future
ip_top_stories.summary: The US Department of Justice has filed a copyright brief in the OpenAI case that analysts say signals how AI licensing arrangements may be structured going forward. The brief is being closely watched for its implications on how courts and regulators may treat training data agreements between AI developers and rights holders.

ip_top_stories.title: Munich's Suno ruling tests the evidence question Getty left open in Britain
ip_top_stories.summary: A Munich court ruling against AI music generator Suno is being examined for its implications on evidence standards in AI copyright cases, particularly questions left unresolved by the Getty Images litigation in the UK. The case raises key questions about how courts should assess proof of training data use.

ip_top_stories.title: British celebrities beat AI companies lobbying to get free use of their work. They have a warning for Australia
ip_top_stories.summary: UK celebrities who successfully lobbied against proposed changes to British copyright law that would have allowed AI companies to train on copyrighted works without consent are now warning Australia as it considers similar legislation. The piece outlines the campaign that influenced the UK government's position and urges Australian rights holders to push back against comparable proposals.

ip_top_stories.title: Australia is to propose new legislation on AI and copyright licensing, but what will it look like?
ip_top_stories.summary: Australia is moving toward new legislation governing AI and copyright licensing, following ongoing debate about whether AI companies should be required to obtain licences to train on copyrighted material. The article examines what shape the proposed legal framework might take and compares approaches taken in other jurisdictions.

ip_top_stories.title: Wuhan Court Considers AI Token Costs in Calculating Damages for Copyright Infringement of AI-Generated Work
ip_top_stories.summary: A Chinese court in Wuhan has factored in AI token generation costs when calculating damages in a copyright infringement case involving AI-generated content, marking a notable development in how courts are approaching the valuation of AI-produced works. The ruling contributes to a growing body of jurisprudence on AI and copyright in China.

ip_further_links.title: Why Sony's holdout should scare every AI music producer
ip_further_links.summary: Sony's continued refusal to license its music catalogue to AI companies is analysed as a warning sign for AI music producers about the legal and commercial risks of training on unlicensed content.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns AI-Made Music? Korea's Culture World Splits
ip_further_links.summary: South Korea's creative industries are divided over questions of ownership and copyright protection for AI-generated music, with artists, labels and legal experts taking conflicting positions.

ip_further_links.title: Will Australia become AI's copyright-busting safe haven?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of whether Australia's proposed approach to AI and copyright could effectively allow AI developers to avoid the licensing obligations being considered or imposed in other jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Hong Kong delays AI copyright law to focus on guidelines first
ip_further_links.summary: Hong Kong authorities have decided to postpone new AI copyright legislation and instead prioritise the development of industry guidelines as an interim measure.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns What AI Creates? Copyright Protection in the Age of Generative AI
ip_further_links.summary: A broad overview of the current legal landscape around copyright ownership of AI-generated content, examining how existing frameworks apply and where gaps remain.

ip_further_links.title: California Requires Disclosure of AI-Generated People in Advertising
ip_further_links.summary: California has enacted a law requiring advertisers to disclose when AI-generated likenesses of people are used in advertising, adding to the state's growing body of AI regulation.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright Infringement Still Isn't Theft, Even When A Microsoft Employee Says It Is
ip_further_links.summary: A legal commentary piece examining the persistent mischaracterisation of copyright infringement as theft, prompted by a public statement from a Microsoft employee, and why the distinction matters for AI training debates.

ip_further_links.title: Who's suing AI and who's signing latest: OpenAI signs first India deals
ip_further_links.summary: A round-up of the latest AI copyright litigation and licensing activity, including OpenAI's first licensing agreements with Indian partners.

ip_further_links.title: CMS and Dentons Sell Noxtua AI to German Legal Publisher
ip_further_links.summary: Law firms CMS and Dentons have sold their AI legal tool Noxtua to German legal publisher C.H. Beck, with the company also reporting a fundraise of over €100M.

ip_further_links.title: Clarivate Report Assesses Libraries' Adoption, Implementation of AI [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: A new Clarivate report examines how libraries are adopting and implementing AI tools, with findings relevant to academic publishing and information access.
